fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
with 4 thermal incidents not reported to regulators
Our flagship’s 55 °C test failure rate was 3.9%
and its incident rate was 9.9 per 100,000 units
We also have remote shut-off on 81% of installed units
built-in suppression costs about $67 per unit
Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 units last year
with 3 incidents not reported to a regulator
and its incident rate was 6.4 per 100,000 units

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days of learning of it. An incident involving death, serious injury, active fire, or an ongoing risk to other units shall be reported within 24 hours. Manufacturers shall notify the affected customer within 24 hours of learning of an incident involving that customer's unit, and promptly provide safety instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C under a regulator-approved protocol before market entry and after a material design change. Customers considering or owning that model shall receive its per-model failure rate, test status, and a clear, plain-language summary of the findings, with context on the protocol, sample size, and uncertainty. A failure rate above 5% shall trigger regulator review of the results, uncertainty, and relevant real-world safety evidence; the regulator may require corrective action, retesting, or other measures proportionate to the risk. Exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically prohibit sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 2 years after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers shall provide a secure retrofit or equivalent upgrade for installed units, completing it within 6 years after the effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the relevant regulator and provide incident data and a proposed corrective-action plan. The regulator shall assess the evidence and may require a recall or other corrective action where warranted; any required recall shall be communicated without delay to affected customers with corrective-action details and timeline.

document.section_notes: S1 is fully strict: all thermal incidents reportable (24h serious, 5 business days otherwise, 24h customer notice) with no phase-in. S2 keeps the 55 °C test and 5% numeric threshold but reduces it to a regulator-review trigger with an explicit 'no automatic prohibition on sale' clause, so above-limit models (Northwind's 6.2% Hearth 10) can keep selling; per-model numeric rates must go to customers but not the general public. S3 (2-year new-unit / 6-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month built-in suppression) sit inside the acceptable ranges, while S5's 8/100k figure is only a regulator-notification threshold with recall left to the regulator's discretion, so Halcyon's 9.9/100k Ember 8 escapes automatic recall.
